chunks: From him, from Sa'dan ibn Muslim, from Is'haq ibn Ammar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

He said: 'Whoever performs one Tawaf of this House, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will write for him six thousand good deeds, erase from him six thousand sins, and elevate for him six thousand levels, so that when he is at the Multazam, Allah will open for him seven doors from the doors of Paradise.'

I said to him, 'May I be sacrificed for you, is all this merit regarding the Tawaf?' He said, 'Yes, and I shall inform you of something superior to that: fulfilling the need of a Muslim is superior to performing Tawaf, and Tawaf, and Tawaf,' until he reached ten.

key_terms.الْمُلْتَزَم: The Multazam (the section of the wall of the Kaaba between the door and the corner where the Yemeni stone is set)
key_terms.قَضَاءُ حَاجَةِ الْمُسْلِمِ: Fulfilling the need of a Muslim

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of performing one Tawaf of the Kaaba and how does it compare to fulfilling a Muslim's need?
ai.summary: In this hadith from Al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) quantifies the spiritual merit of a single Tawaf as erasing sins and elevating ranks, yet elevates 'Qada' al-Hajah' (fulfilling a believer's need) above ten Tawafs, highlighting the Shia emphasis on social solidarity over mere ritual. This comparison underscores the principle that serving the community is a higher form of worship, linking the physical act of pilgrimage with the spiritual duty of mutual support among believers. The narration thus serves as a key text for understanding the balance between individual devotion and communal responsibility in Shia jurisprudence.

en.hubeali: From him, from Sa’dan Bin Muslim, from Is’haq Bin Ammar, (It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullahasws having said: ‘The one who performs Tawaaf of this House (Kabah), one Tawaaf, Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic would Write for him six thousand good deeds and Delete from him six thousand sins, and Elevate for him six thousand levels, to the extent that when he would be by Al-Multazam (back of the Kabah), Allahazwj would Open for him seven Doors from the Doors of the Paradise’.

I said to himasws, ‘May I be sacrificed for youasws! This merit, all of it is regarding the Tawaaf?’ Heasws said: ‘Yes, and Iasws shall inform you with the more superior than that – fulfilling a need of the Muslim is superior than performing a Tawaaf, and a Tawaaf, and a Tawaaf’, until heasws reached ten’.
en.sarwar: 8. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Sa’dan ibn Muslim from Ishaq ibn ‘Ammar from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

“Whoever performs a single Tawaf (walking seven times around the Ka’ba for worship) of this House Allah, the Most Majestic, the Most Holy, writes down for him six thousand good deeds, deletes his six thousand sins, and raises him six thousand degrees in meritorious status until he reaches al-Multazam (a part of Ka’ba) Allah then opens seven doors of paradise for him.’

I then asked, ‘May Allah keep my soul in service for your cause, all these rewards just for one Tawaf (walking seven times around the Ka’ba for worship)?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, and I can tell you something better than this and that is helping the wish of a Muslim to come true. It is better than a Tawaf, a Tawaf. . . . (walking seven times around the Ka’ba for worship), the Imam repeated ten times.’”
